title: genescout: PTEN and MUC16 are reported as unresolved and rank last
description:
After **Load 4-source example** and **Rank genes**, the app shows "2 of 32 genes could not be resolved (ranked at the bottom): PTEN, MUC16". Both are current HGNC symbols and MyGene finds both, but they end up last with no signals, so PTEN drops out of an NF1-associated MPNST review.

## Cause

MyGene returns two Ensembl gene ids for each of these genes, so the `ensembl` field is a list of objects. The second id is on an assembly patch:

```
PTEN   [{"gene": "ENSG00000171862"}, {"gene": "ENSG00000284792"}]   second id on HG2334_PATCH
MUC16  [{"gene": "ENSG00000181143"}, {"gene": "ENSG00000291738"}]   second id on HG2461_PATCH
NF1    {"gene": "ENSG00000196712"}
```

`mygene_parse_hit()` reads it with `pluck_at(hit, "ensembl", "gene")` (`R/tools/mygene.R:177`). On a list of objects that returns `NULL`, so `ensembl_gene` is `NA`. `resolve_genes()` (`R/enrich.R:1726`) counts a gene as resolved only when `ensembl_gene` is set, so both genes are dropped.

## Reproduce

From `apps/genescout`:

```r
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
source("R/http.R")
source("R/tools/mygene.R")
r <- resolve_symbols_batch(c("PTEN", "MUC16", "NF1"))
vapply(r, function(x) x$ensembl_gene, "")
#> [1] NA                NA                "ENSG00000196712"
```

## Possible fix

When `ensembl` is a list, read `gene` from each element and keep the id on the primary assembly (`ENSG00000171862` for PTEN, `ENSG00000181143` for MUC16). A test with this response shape would keep it fixed.

## Where the fix belongs

`apps/sources.yml` pins `samuelbharti/genescout` at `v0.1.5`, and `R/tools/mygene.R` is the same on that repository's `main`. Fix it there, publish a release, then re-vendor.

The same read is in variant-reviewer's `R/api_mygene.R` and in bioclients 0.1.1 (`mygene_gene()` and `mygene_genes()` return `NA` for PTEN's `ensembl_gene`).

title: genescout: Analyze with specialists blocks the whole app while it runs
description:
On the deployed GeneScout (`apps/genescout`), one run of **Analyze with specialists** stops the app from answering anyone else, and it stays that way after the browser that started the run closes.

## Steps

1. Open https://posit-genescout.share.connect.posit.cloud/ and set the provider to Google (Gemini) with a key and the provider default model.
2. Click **Load 4-source example**, then **Rank genes** (32 candidates, NF1-associated cancer (MPNST)).
3. Click **Analyze with specialists**.

## Observed

On 2026-10-07 I clicked it at about 18:08 UTC. After 2 minutes the "Running specialists on the top candidates..." bar had barely moved, and I closed the browser at 18:10 UTC. From 18:18 UTC the app did not load: a new browser waited 4 minutes for the page, and every request from 18:25 to 19:09 UTC timed out with no response. Since 19:10 UTC it answers 503 "Content Unavailable" after about a minute. The other gallery apps answered in about a second over the same period.

## Cause

`modules/mod_results.R:330` runs the specialists as `withProgress(genescout_llm_run(run_specialists, ...))`. `genescout_llm_run()` in `R/llm_offload.R` hands the work to a mirai daemon and then waits for it on line 116:

```r
res <- m[] # blocks on an interrupt-safe nanonext receive, not inside libcurl
```

The model calls run in the daemon, but the main R process sits in `m[]` until they finish, so it serves no other session in the meantime. Nothing stops the run when the session that started it ends. If the daemon fails, line 121 runs the same work again in the main process.

**Curate with AI** (`modules/mod_results.R:250`) and the input agent (`modules/mod_review.R:307`) go through the same function, so they block the app in the same way for as long as their model calls take.

## Possible fix

- Run these steps as a `shiny::ExtendedTask` around the mirai call, so the session waits for its own result and the process keeps serving everyone else.
- Give each run a time limit, and cancel it when the session ends.

## Where the fix belongs

`apps/genescout` is vendored: `apps/sources.yml` pins it to `samuelbharti/genescout` at `v0.1.5`, and `R/llm_offload.R` is the same on that repository's `main`. Fix it there, publish a release, then re-vendor.

The current deployment needs a restart on Connect Cloud.

description:


title: This repo is the source of truth for the four lifescience apps
description:
DE Explorer, Signature Scoring, Drug Perturbation and Genome Explorer live in apps/ here. This repo is their only source now. posit-dev/lifescience-shiny-gallery is where they came from originally, but it isn't the source anymore.

Updates to these four apps will land as PRs directly against this repo. That's intentional. They're simple apps and don't change often, so the vendoring workflow the other five apps use isn't worth setting up here.

One thing to fix as part of the sanitization pass: each app still has a navlink in its UI pointing to posit-dev/lifescience-shiny-gallery (see app.R in each app folder). That repo is private, so once these apps deploy, the link goes nowhere for anyone outside Posit. Point it here instead, or remove it.

Open question: should these four stay here, or move to their own repo with a real sanitization pass, then get vendored back in like the other five? Since they change so rarely, keeping them here seems like less work than setting up a full vendoring relationship for four apps. I'd lean toward keeping them here, unless one needs its own citation or DOI later.

variant-reviewer does not start on Connect Cloud: .Rprofile reads repos["biobouncer"]
description:
`apps/variant-reviewer` has never started on Connect Cloud. Every deployment uploads and publishes, and then the application fails at R startup. The four other deployed applications are unaffected.

## The error

From the Connect Cloud publishing log, on every deployment:

```
ERROR: Error in if (is.na(repos["biobouncer"])) { : argument is of length zero
ERROR: Worker error: exit status 1
ERROR: Failed to publish content: Your application failed to start.
```

## Cause

`apps/variant-reviewer/.Rprofile`, which `manifest.json` ships:

```r
source("renv/activate.R")

# biobouncer (input validation) is published on r-universe, not CRAN. Keep its
# repo alongside CRAN so install/restore/snapshot can find it.
local({
  repos <- getOption("repos")
  if (is.na(repos["biobouncer"])) {
    repos["biobouncer"] <- "https://samuelbharti.r-universe.dev"
    options(repos = repos)
  }
})
```

The guard assumes `getOption("repos")` returns something subsettable. On Connect Cloud it is empty, so `repos["biobouncer"]` is length zero, `is.na()` of that is `logical(0)`, and `if (logical(0))` is an error. R startup fails, so the application never runs. It works locally only because a local session always has `repos` set.

`length(...) == 0` rather than `is.na(...)` would fix it, or `!("biobouncer" %in% names(repos))`.

None of the other four deployed applications has an `.Rprofile`.

## Where the fix belongs

`.Rprofile` is vendored. `apps/sources.yml` maps this directory to `samuelbharti/variant-reviewer` at `v2.3.1`, and the next `vendor-apps.yml` run discards anything changed here, so the repository rule applies: **fix the source repository, publish a release, then re-vendor.** I have read-only access to that repository and cannot file there.

## State in this repository, meanwhile

The tile in `apps.yml` now carries `deploy: false` and **no** `content_id`, so:

- the workflow does not deploy it, and no job fails for it;
- `showcase.ejs` shows no "View app" button, so the card does not link to an application that cannot start.

Content `01a06d89-069b-1b9b-e8a7-be4da970cbcf` exists on Connect Cloud and is waiting for the fix. Restoring the `content_id` and removing `deploy: false` is all that is needed once a release lands.

## How this went unnoticed

Two reasons, both now closed:

1. **`deployApp()` does not signal a failed publish.** It prints `Deployment failed with error: ...` and returns `FALSE` invisibly. `deploy_app.R` ignored the value and exited 0, so the deployment step would have been **green in CI for an application that never started**. The script now stops on a falsy return; verified against this application, which exits 1.
2. **A 200 from the address is not proof the application works.** Connect Cloud answers for content whose application failed to start, so `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` reported success. Checking the body is the real test: the four working applications return 35–190 kB of Shiny and bslib assets, and this one returned 61 bytes.

title: Reread the CAUTION in README.md: gene-list-builder is described as private but is deployed publicly
description:
The CAUTION block at the top of `README.md` needs a human who knows the sanitization status. I cannot settle it from the repository, and it is the one open item with a disclosure angle.

## The contradiction

The block says:

> The site shows screenshots of private applications. `gene-list-builder` is private. The four `lifescience-shiny-gallery` applications are Posit-internal, because that repository is not public, although its license is MIT. The README of `comp-bio-apps` says that this material needs a sanitization pass first.

But `gene-list-builder` now has, in `apps.yml`:

- a public GitHub repository, <https://github.com/samuelbharti/gene-list-builder>
- a DOI, <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21950640>
- a public deployment at <https://posit-gene-list-builder.share.connect.posit.cloud/>, with `default_robots_policy: allow_all`, so search engines are invited to index it

So either the CAUTION is stale and `gene-list-builder` became public at some point, or an application that is meant to be private is currently serving publicly and indexably.

## Which it is, and what to do

If the CAUTION is stale: correct that sentence, and check the rest of the block at the same time. The two numbered problems and the closing line have all been overtaken by events to some degree, since the applications now deploy automatically.

If the CAUTION is right: `gene-list-builder` needs `deploy: false` in `apps.yml`, its `content_id` removed, its content deleted from Connect Cloud, and its links reviewed.

## Not in question

The four `lifescience-shiny-gallery` applications (`de-explorer`, `signature-scoring`, `drug-perturbation`, `genome-explorer`) all carry `deploy: false` and have no `content_id`. They are not deployed and have no public address. Whoever rereads this should confirm that is still the intent, but nothing has published them.

title: deploy_matrix.py: a quoted "false" in deploy silently deployed a held-back app
description:
Filed as a record of a class of bug this repository is exposed to, and of the test that now prevents it. Fixed by #28; kept open only until that merges.

## What was wrong

`.github/scripts/deploy_matrix.py` decides which applications deploy, from the `deploy` field in `apps.yml`. It read the field without testing its type:

```python
deploy = tile.get("deploy", True)
...
if not deploy:
    continue   # held back
```

A quoted value is a string, and a non-empty string is true in Python:

```yaml
deploy: "false"    # a string, not a boolean
```

So `deploy: "false"` deployed the application. Confirmed by experiment before the fix: quoting the value on all four `lifescience-shiny-gallery` tiles flipped them from `HOLD` to deploying.

## Why it mattered here

`deploy: false` is the mechanism that holds back the four applications from `posit-dev/lifescience-shiny-gallery`, which the CAUTION in `README.md` says need a sanitization pass before they get a public address. A deployment publishes to a public URL, and now also to search engines. So a single pair of quotation marks, of the kind a person adds while tidying YAML, was enough to publish material that is deliberately unpublished. Nothing would have complained.

## What the review comment found

The `apps.yml` job in `checks.yml` runs the program, and the program's exit status is the only assertion it makes. The question was: what does that actually assert? The answer was three presence tests and no type tests. An assertion with no test is a comment, and a program used as a test needs its own.

## What #28 does about it

`deploy_matrix.py` and `R/check.R` now test the type and the shape of every field they read, and report all problems at once rather than the first:

| Field | Test |
|---|---|
| `deploy` | must be a real boolean; a string or a number is an error, and it is tested even on a tile with no `app`, so a typo fails wherever it appears |
| `content_id` | must be a string with the shape of a Connect Cloud content id |
| `app` | must be a string usable as a hostname label, and must name a directory in `apps/` that holds a `manifest.json` |
| `pcc-account` | must be present and hostname-safe as soon as a tile below the category deploys |
| the file | must be a list of categories, each holding a list of tile mappings |

`.github/scripts/test_deploy_matrix.py` covers those with 27 cases, including `deploy: "false"` specifically. `checks.yml` runs the tests **before** the program, so a test that stopped working cannot leave the job green.

## To reproduce the guard

```bash
python .github/scripts/test_deploy_matrix.py
```

Or by hand: quote a `deploy: false` in `apps.yml` and run either program. Both now fail with `must be true or false`.
